bundles.evidenceText: therefore it follows logically that the transcendent cause of the universe is an unembodied mind
bundles.rationale: The expressed proposition is that, given a transcendent cause with the preceding description, eliminating abstract objects identifies it as an unembodied mind or personal creator. That proposition can remain true even if a finite beginning and need for a cause do not imply an uncaused, timeless, spaceless, immaterial cause; it presupposes rather than supports that inference. The no-contact tuple therefore fits and excludes option-2's support for pro subsidiary 1.

bundles.evidenceText: the rational attitude in the absence of a very strong case for the existence of a Christian God is to believe that there is no such thing
bundles.rationale: The expressed proposition is that, because the specifically Christian God claim competes with thousands of alternatives, absent an overwhelmingly strong case the rational attitude is withholding or rejection, including atheism. This supports the con motion bridge's complete conclusion that belief in the Christian God should be withheld or rejected. Option-2 is excluded because the move does not assert the narrower central proposition that all five evidential lines fail through underdetermination and contrary empirical evidence.

bundles.evidenceText: I don't think you could infer obviously infinite power from fine-tuning
bundles.rationale: The expressed proposition limits what fine-tuning and the other arguments identify: they warrant at most enormous power, not infinite power. That limitation supports the con subsidiary-2 proposition that fine-tuning does not identify an omniperfect Christian God. Option-2 is excluded because this concession can remain true whether or not design explains fine-tuning better than physical necessity or chance, so it does not support the pro subsidiary-2 comparison.
